newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs steady, Bund spread edges out.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs steady, Bund spread edges out.

text.p: Belgian bonds held steady in calm business on Monday as players took a step back, with last Friday's U.S. monthly jobs data now out of the way, to consider future direction.
By 0935 GMT the 10-year OLO yield had edged down to 5.74 percent from 5.75 percent on Friday, its premium over equivalent Bund yields widening one basis point to seven.
"We have a slow start for a Monday morning," one dealer said. "Prices could come under pressure due to a heavy load that might come onto the market after tommorow's OLO exchange auction," he added.
The Treasury will offer OLOs maturing in April 1999, March 2001, March 2005 and March 2007 - the 10-year benchmark - in exchange for May 1997 and August 1997 maturities.
Several dealers expected higher yields in the weeks ahead, with the yield spread over Bunds likely to remain in its current range.

One expected the market to become increasingly nervous ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve's next FOMC meeting on interest rate policy, scheduled for March 25. "I think the 10-year yield could go up to 5.80 percent or 5.85 percent before then, but not higher" he said.
